name: Ruoxi (Anna) Shang
title: PhD Candidate, Human-Centered Design & Engineering — University of Washington

details: Committee: Gary Hsieh, Chirag Shah, Tim Althoff, David McDonald
Undergraduate research in applied ML, computer vision, and scientific prediction.

experience.title: Research Fellow
details: Designed **RiskBench**, an agentic safety benchmark that decomposes risk into six independently variable dimensions, enabling diagnosis of agent behavior across various risk mechanisms.

Built an agent trace augmentation pipeline that varies safety-relevant factors such as trajectory stage and availability of safe alternatives, allowing controlled measurement of unsafe action, over-refusal, and sensitivity to scenario perturbations.
Developed rubric-based LLM-judge evaluations that enable granular and precise classification of agent responses beyond safe/unsafe binary labels.

Trained linear probes on model activations from benchmark trajectories; found that risk perception was linearly decodable, but activation steering did not reliably change behavior, suggesting a gap between risk representation and safe action.

experience.title: Research Intern
details: Designed **ASPECT**, a framework that distills workplace interaction data into interpretable, editable profiles for personalizing social agents at inference time through a structured taxonomy inspired by constructs from psychometric instruments.

Built an evaluation pipeline using **90 days of real workplace communication data** and direct human feedback to assess the method's social appropriateness, systematic biases, and alignment with human preferences. _Manuscript and patent application under review._

experience.title: Graduate Researcher
details: Studied the impact of AI on knowledge workers across data analysis, peer review, and teaching feedback, identifying both opportunities and challenges.
Designed evaluation methods for both general capabilities and context-dependent usage of LLMs.
Developed and validated measurement instruments for trust and reliance in AI agents.

experience.title: Research Intern
experience.collaborators: Steven Drucker, Bongshin Lee, Dave Brown
details: Investigated how data analysts use and verify LLM-generated analyses in realistic end-to-end data-analysis workflows.

Designed and ran studies with industry-experienced analysts to evaluate how they understand, trust, and verify AI-generated analyses, identifying failure modes in human oversight and design requirements for AI-assisted analysis tools. _Co-authored a paper accepted at CHI 2024._

experience.title: Data Science and User Research Intern
experience.collaborators: Mantas Lilis, Joshua Noble, Justin Lawyer
details: Designed ML model-diagnostics workflows for industry-experienced data scientists, identifying friction points in model failure detection, debugging, and explanation.
Translated technical failure modes into actionable product features, contributing to the roadmap for ML debugging tools.

impact.title: Research Lead, Healthcare Equity Study
impact.organization: UW Medicine Office of Healthcare Equity
details: Led a 10-researcher team studying equity concerns across UW Medicine communities; designed psychologically safe protocols for **16 focus groups with 71 stakeholders** including patients, students, residents, faculty, and staff.
Synthesized access barriers, invisible DEI labor, burnout, and distrust in bias-reporting systems into a causal-loop map and institutional recommendations for more accountable support structures.

impact.title: Teaching & Mentorship
details: Mentored **50+ student teams** in graduate project-based courses on designing for human-centered AI systems and responsible deployment.
